title: Cops raid office of RFK Jr. allies planning “unethical” vaccine trial on babies
gist: Guinea-Bissau police raided the Bandim Health Project offices and seized hepatitis B vaccines meant for a CDC-funded newborn trial that international experts call unethical. The trial has not been authorized by the country's government despite renewed US funding reports.

insights.claim: Judicial police in Guinea-Bissau searched the Bandim Health Project offices in Bissau and seized a batch of hepatitis B vaccines intended for newborn vaccination, opening an investigation into the Danish researchers.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Local enforcement is now a real obstacle to US-funded research that bypasses host-country approval.
insights.quote: Police in Guinea-Bissau raided the offices of Danish researchers on Monday, seizing doses of hepatitis B vaccine

insights.claim: Police stressed that the seizure is an investigative step and does not itself imply irregularities in the vaccines' quality, safety or effectiveness, so the raid is not evidence of product problems.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Avoid over-reading the raid as proof of wrongdoing; the legal process is early.

insights.claim: The Guinea-Bissau health minister said the government has not authorized the trial and called reports that it would proceed 'not even remotely true', undercutting the US funding plan.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Without host-government sign-off the funded trial cannot proceed regardless of US backing.

insights.claim: The CDC under Kennedy awarded an unsolicited $1.6 million grant in December to the Danish researchers, and Rolling Stone reported another $1.6 million was set aside in late September, showing persistent federal backing despite the January halt.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: US public-health grantmaking under this HHS leadership is a recurring controversy and reputational risk for related agencies and institutions.

insights.claim: The researchers, repeatedly praised by Kennedy, are themselves under investigation by Danish authorities for alleged scientific misconduct, which adds legal exposure to the program.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Sponsor association with contested researchers raises odds of further scandal and funding reversals.

insights.claim: The trial design would potentially expose thousands of newborns to hepatitis B, risking lifelong infection leading to cirrhosis, cancer and premature death, which is why international experts label it unethical.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Ethical objections, not just procedural ones, drive the pressure that halted the plan in January.
insights.locator: Plans for the trial were halted
